reviewCorrectionsVerified: New source and compiled-runtime pins are rechecked before selection of the release.
Recovery accepts only an exactly owned installed drop-in when normalizing the original unit identity.
Drop-in identity and exact bytes are rechecked after awaited service stops and before rename.
Incomplete cleanup leaves a nonterminal active recovery state, permitting bounded reviewed recovery again.

mutationBoundary.localEffects: Only controlled synthetic fixture files and safe review artifacts. Disposable filesystem cleanup target was resolved and checked inside the owned review directory.

coordination.author: backend_acceptance
coordination.overlap: The actual recovery body is tested here. Negative cutover tests replace recovery with a labeled port; the other reviewer tests successful/signal cutover and cleanup independently.

diagnostics.history: Earlier local harness development attempts are retained under .local/private-staging-recovery-review-20261015. They include WinError1314 for OS symlink creation, a fixture method/name collision and fixture metadata updates for newly strict PID/start/intent validation. They are not operator regressions.
diagnostics.negativeBaseline: The attempted before-poststop source capture already contained the correction; its pass is not represented as an expected-failure baseline.

limits: This is local function/control-flow acceptance, not Linux UID, actual signals, real parent death or service recovery acceptance.
The Linux private-file reader and one symlink observation are explicit ports in these tests; no POSIX permission claim follows.
Cutover fingerprint and external service observations use synthetic ports. Real clone, stopped-state preservation and activation still require their own operation evidence.
No public launch, new supplier/TDX functionality, full-suite pass or percentage increase is established.
